channel.title: Yorkshire Gigs Events
channel.description: Upcoming Yorkshire events in the Gigs category.

item.title: The Zawose Queens
item.description: Pendo and Leah Zawose, two women from a famous Tanzanian musical family, take their place as lead vocalists and performers. Their music is rooted in traditional singing and instrumentation, with contemporary touches of leftfield pop and synth-funk.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Chopin Nocturnes
item.description: "Poet of the piano” Pavel Kolesnikov is one of the world’s most exciting young pianists. Lauded for his amazing ability to cast new light on familiar repertoire, he makes his Music in the Round debut with a tour through Chopin's complete Nocturnes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: SPO play Mahler, Farrenc and Bottesini
item.description: Sheffield Philharmonic Orchestra play Mahler’s Symphony no.5, Farrenc overture no.2 and Bottesini concerto for double bass.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Live Music – Tribute to the Stars of the Decades
item.description: Enjoy an unforgettable evening of live music as Daz Longthorne performs the greatest hits from the 1950s through to the 1980s. Featuring classics from Elvis Presley, Neil Diamond, Elton John, […] \n

item.title: Sylvie + Ursula
item.description: The duo of rising London-based vocalist Sylvie Noble and BBC Young Jazz Musician of the Year 2025 Ursula Harrison (double bass) bring their beautifully poised, playful, resonant and captivating music to Jazz at The Lescar.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Zoe Rahman Trio
item.description: Zoe Rahman presents new music with her world-class trio. Based on themes of voyage, migration and the sea and taking inspiration from Hull, the music is also deeply connected to Zoe’s family history. In association with Sheffield Jazz.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bellot Ensemble
item.description: The award-winning vibrant, period instrument group present Heroines of the Seicento.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Candlelit Mozart Requiem
item.description: Come and hear the Cathedral Choir with West Riding Ensemble perform Mozart's Requiem, Coronation Mass, and Ave verum corpus in a candlelit setting.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Grass
item.description: Screening of the silent masterpiece Grass (1925) with live music by Peyman Yazdanian and Adib Rostami.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Maddalena Ghezzi, Ruth Goller, Maria Chiara Argirò
item.description: Jazz at The Lescar present a trio of leading creative musicians from the London scene. With fearless, unique and explorative new music mixing ethereal vocals, atmospheric synths sounds, and visceral bass.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lambchop
item.description: Brudenell presents: an intimate piano performance from Lambchop. Initially indebted to traditional country, the band’s music has subsequently moved through a range of influences including post-rock, soul and lounge music.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Carmen's Voice
item.description: Carmen was never a love story. This November, Atelier Armonico presents Carmen’s Voice, a new adaptation of Bizet’s iconic opera shaped by women’s lived experiences. Performed in English and featuring a 12-piece chamber orchestra.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Rheingans Sisters
item.description: Winners of BBC Radio 2 Folk Award present their uniquely blended sound of fiddles, voices, feet, banjos, guitar, synths and the powerful bass drones of the medieval tambourin à cordes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Snuts
item.description: Scottish indie-rockers The Snuts bring their signature sound to the Octagon, following the release of the highly anticipated album Joy in Short Moments. Supported by Liverpudlian friends The Kairos.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: A Journey Through Nordic Music
item.description: Join a panel of musicians and experts who will shine a light on some of the composers and music featuring across Northern Lights, Music in the Round's weekend of elemental music from the frozen north.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Music from Iceland
item.description: A dazzling portrait of contemporary Icelandic music ranging from celebrated glacial works by Anna Thorvaldsdóttir and Oscar-winning Hildur Guðnadóttir, to new arrangements of Björk and Ólafur Arnalds’ haunting music for Broadchurch.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bob Dylan
item.description: Widely acknowledged as one of the most important figures of the modern day and one of the greatest and most influential songwriters of all time, Bob Dylan has reshaped popular music by elevating lyric writing to a profound literary art form.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Pitchblack Playback: My Bloody Valentine - Loveless
item.description: Immerse yourself in My Bloody Valentine's shoegaze-defining classic on a powerful cinema sound system. Pitchblack Playback's listening session in the dark celebrates the album's 35th anniversary.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Sibelius & Grieg
item.description: Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 performs masterpieces and miniatures for strings and piano by two giants of Nordic classicism.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Engegård Quartet
item.description: Norway’s multi-award-winning Engegård Quartet brings its customary boldness, energy and freshness to Sheffield in a concert of Mozart, Beethoven and Grieg.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Adam Hopper & The Wimps
item.description: Sheffield based Adam Hopper and his band play a blend of mellow alternative pop and anti-folk. Drawing inspiration from 70s art-rock, 90s lo-fi and Americana, their sound moves from intimate folk passages to weirder, psych-inspired freak-outs.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Norwegian Folk
item.description: Formed under the midnight sun in the Lofoten Islands, Norway’s leading string quartet brings the rugged soul of the country to the stage, with arrangements of traditional joiks, haunting psalms and spirited bridal marches.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Alex Lukashevsky + Alex Rex
item.description: Celebrated legend of Toronto’s music scene, known for his boundary-pushing approach to folk and avant-garde music, twists rock music into strange and brilliant new shapes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Snowman + Live Score
item.description: Unite the Union Brass Band present a special festive performance of the Christmas classic with a live score.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven Appassionata
item.description: Tim Horton performs an afternoon concert for Music in the Round, launching his a journey through Beethoven’s staggering achievements for piano, with works including his celebrated Appassionata sonata.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Reich: Electric Counterpoint
item.description: Scottish guitarist Sean Shibe presents a tour of four centuries of music, including Bach’s first cello suite, Steve Reich’s masterpiece Electric Counterpoint and a recent commission by the UK’s leading contemporary composer Thomas Adès.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Arbrevyn
item.description: Arbrevyn perform a Christmas special concert. Featuring Cornish carols alongside more local carols and some of their favourite repertoire.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: New Voices
item.description: Sheffield Chamber Orchestra present a varied introduction to the richness of orchestral music. From Mendelssohn’s enchanted Shakespearean forest to Dvořák’s Czech dances, Handel’s Baroque elegance and Farrenc’s powerful Romantic symphony.
item.location: All Saints Church, Ringinglow Road, S11 7PP

item.title: Lacross Club
item.description: Welsh punk band Lacross Club play stupid-on-purpose, gloriously unsubtle, dumb rock-n-roll. Their psychobilly infused garage rock is a vehicle for tales about the pub, beer and hangovers. “My head is poundin’, I spent a hundred pounds in a pub.”
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Festive Festival
item.description: A joy-filled gathering dedicated at Victoria and The Mowbray. With festive sing-alongs and choirs, makers' stalls, coffee, feasting, Christmas cocktails, and more.
item.location: The Victoria and The Mowbray, 1 Rowland Street, Neepsend, S3 8DE

item.title: Beer and Carols
item.description: Taking you back to Christmas singing assembly. Grab a drink and belt out all your favourite carols with a Cathedral full of people who remember every word (or at least the chorus!).
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Sheffield Beatles Project
item.description: Celebrating their 10th year, the 30-piece Sheffield Beatles Project return for their annual Christmas show, recreating the music of the Fab Four in minute detail. They’ll perform the complete Magical Mystery Tour album, plus favourites and rarities.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Hanging Stars
item.description: Drawing influence from The Byrds, Teenage Fanclub and Big Star, London's Hanging Stars make music full of chiming guitars, four-part harmonies and irresistible melodies. Expect sun-drenched psychedelic folk and beautifully crafted rock songs.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Belle and Sebastian
item.description: One of the UK’s most beloved indie pop groups, known for their delicate melodies, captivating storytelling and achingly personal lyrics. This December, they’re celebrating 30 years since the release of their landmark album If You’re Feeling Sinister.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Christmas Eve
item.description: Christmas Eve at The Piece Hall Visit us on Christmas Eve and enjoy a festive day at The Piece Hall. Explore three floors of independent shops, bars and cafés and enjoy a ride on the carousel, open throughout the day. The much-loved Halifax Minster Choir will be performing at midday, followed by the Queensbury Brass...
